title: Python: LIT, a local or module name whose every binding is a literal or comprehension of one builtin type resolves as external (DEC-303 (a22) item 3)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3, group LIT, verbatim: 'LIT, every binding is a literal or comprehension of one builtin type: admitted as resolved-external under item 2, with the nonlocal and global provisos.' Governing line (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope; for a local, writes through nonlocal in nested scopes count as bindings; for a module-level name, writes through global in the same module count; a write from outside the module (m.X = ...) is the accepted blind spot. Probed on dev ed37361: x = [] then x.append(1), x = {} then x.get(1), s = 'a' then s.join(...), a list or dict comprehension, and two same-type literal bindings all land in receiver-needs-inference today, so LIT is unbuilt. Part of the DEC-303 (a23) build order (K1, LIT, M1, R4, ALIAS, TS, Q1, then (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. Reuse the GCLI-108 findings: one binding enumeration (lookupBindings) with the global and nonlocal provisos; known follow-ups there (lookupBindings and globalNames; rule 38 and loops) stay out of scope.

acceptanceCriteria.text: a name whose every binding is a literal or comprehension of ONE builtin type (list, dict, set, tuple, str, bytes, int, float and the comprehension forms) resolves a one-segment method call as resolved-external, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins

a second binding of a different type, or of anything that is not such a literal, a nonlocal write from a nested scope, or a global write for a module-level name leaves the call unresolved, each with a fixture
each rule has a mutation check that goes red, and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with any in-repo edge it creates or removes named

implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a22) item 3 LIT: every binding is a literal or comprehension of one builtin type; resolved-external under item 2 with the nonlocal and global provisos). PROBE on dev ed37361: unbuilt, every literal-bound receiver was receiver-needs-inference. SCOPE RULINGS (leader, from the rule text): [*x] is a list and is accepted; implicit-concatenated strings are one str (or one bytes) and are accepted; a binding set mixing int and float is TWO types and stays unresolved (no numeric family); the forms the task does not list stay unresolved: None, True, False, f-strings and template strings, a negated number, an imaginary number, a generator expression, a conditional or binary expression, a parenthesised display, a call, a name. BUILT in src/python/calls.ts: (1) BindingRhs gains kind literal with the type; literalType maps list, dictionary, set, tuple displays and their comprehensions, integer, float (imaginary refused), string (prefix f or t refused, b is bytes, else str) and concatenated_string (every part the same type) from syntax alone; handleAssignment records it. (2) enumerableBindings(name, scope, site) is the one enumeration K1 and LIT share: null when the starting scope is a class body that binds the name (the class or globals are read, never an enclosing function), and null when a scope between the use and the bindings declares global for the name unless the bindings are the module s own; writes through global and nonlocal from other scopes were already moved onto the target scope by applyScopeRedirects. isSplatParameter was refactored onto it, no behaviour change (K1 fixtures unchanged). (3) isLiteralBound: every binding must be an unannotated assignment whose right-hand side is a literal of the SAME type; any rebind, augmented assignment, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, tuple or star target, annotated binding (an annotation can name an in-repo class), type alias, parameter or conditional rebind is a second kind of binding and refuses. One segment only. del is no binding and is pinned as such (the call after a del raises, so the claim is vacuous). The existing rule 29c test that pinned a literal-bound global as receiver-needs-inference now pins resolved-external, with a twin pinning a call-bound name unresolved. FIXTURES: describe LIT (11 tests) covering 16 literal forms x function, module and module-name-in-function, same-type and different-type sets, 17 unlisted forms, 19 second-binding shapes each refused with twins, parameters and lambda defaults, global and nonlocal writes with same-type twins and read-only twins, a global between the use and the binding, class-body shapes, no reach to an in-repo method of the same name with a constructed-C twin, and two segments. RED BEFORE: 8 of 11 fail on the dev source. MUTATION CHECKS: 23 mutants, each red after adding the 1.5j and str-plus-bytes fixtures (two survivors found and killed that way); the interpolation test and the kind-is-assign test were removed as equivalent (tree-sitter marks an interpolating string with an f prefix, and only an assignment carries a literal rhs). PER-SITE MEASURE, instrumented origin/dev ed37361 vs the branch, five pins, multiset diff, entry counts equal: 225 sites move receiver-needs-inference to external (flask 72, jinja 60, httpx 34, rich 29, tqdm 30), 0 in-repo edges created or removed, 0 other changes. A random 10-site spot check against the source showed literal-bound receivers (args = [], stack = [..], tqdm_args = {..}). NOT MEASURED: precision on labelled sites; sites in class bodies (refused by design); the cost of the class-body refusal. Gates: typecheck, lint, format:check, bun test 848 pass.

REVIEW ROUND 1 (Opus, #167 at 6ba7a191), amends the build note: (1) a module-level star import is a binding statement in the module's own text that importStatementNames does not record, so x = [] plus from m import * (m exporting x) read as a list: fixed in enumerableBindings by a new starMayBind (a complete star that exports the name, or any partial or unknown star, refuses, as rule 37 does) when the bindings are the module's; K1 is unaffected (a splat binding never lives at module scope, import * in a function is a SyntaxError). Fixtures: a complete exporting star, a star before the literal, an unresolved star, each refused at module level and in a function, with twins (a complete star without x, no star). (2) target shapes pinned as second bindings: (x) = ..., ((x)) = ..., [x] = ..., (x, n) = ..., a = x = ..., except* as, async with-as, async for; match and type as plain identifiers resolve. 3 mutants added (star check off, complete exports ignored, partial ignored), each red; 26 in all. Corpus: 0 of the 225 moved sites are in a file with a module-level star import; re-measure unchanged, 225 sites receiver-needs-inference to external, 0 in-repo edges. bun test 850 pass. FOLLOW-UPS, named and not fixed: PEP 695 type parameters (def f[x](), class K[x]:) are not recorded as bindings; globals()[x] and exec are not enumerable (the same class as the accepted m.X blind spot of (a22) item 2); rule 6d knownClassOf has the same star-import gap (x = C() plus from m import *).
